statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107816 is MariaDB advisory GHSA-wfqg-88r5-55f6: https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-wfqg-88r5-55f6 . The qc_info plugin's qc_info_fill_table in plugin/qc_info/qc_info.cc locates the schema name inside the query cache key by the statement text length, which is wrong when the statement contains NUL bytes. Reading information_schema.query_cache_info after such a query was cached could then read beyond the end of the key buffer. MariaDB fixed it in 11.8.9 (and 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 12.3.3 and 13.0.2) with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/0931994096b84ecc9ffc8eb3517c7e09e6e8631e (MDEV-40670), which limits the schema name length to the bytes left in the key. Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 does not include it. DHI backports the commit's qc_info.cc change unmodified (its new regression test embeds raw NUL bytes and is not carried), and the fixed version is the first build that carries it. We compared all four published builds of 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 on amd64 and arm64, reading function symbols from the matching -dbgsym packages. In query_cache_info.so from the mariadb-server package, qc_info_fill_table grows from 1628 to 1660 bytes on amd64 and from 1512 to 1524 bytes on arm64 between the build before the fix and the fixed build, the only function in that plugin whose size changes. The two later builds ship the same query_cache_info.so as the fixed build (identical build ID) on both architectures. The fixed build's changelog lists this CVE.
